result:
If I could change the world with one single adjustment, I would make every human being *radically* more curious and less certain.

Not kinder (kindness without curiosity becomes performative), not smarter (intelligence without curiosity becomes arrogance), but *curious*.

Imagine a world where:
- People defaulted to "I wonder why they believe that" instead of "They're wrong/stupid/evil"
- Leaders asked better questions than they gave answers
- Education rewarded genuine inquiry over test scores
- We treated our own beliefs as provisional hypotheses rather than sacred identities

Most of humanity's worst behaviors (tribalism, dogmatism, cruelty, stagnation) ultimately stem from the refusal to stay curious when it's uncomfortable. The single lever that pulls almost every other good outcome is rebuilding that muscle: the instinctive drive to understand before judging, to explore before concluding, to wonder before defending.

Curiosity is the only known antidote to certainty that doesn't require force. It scales. It compounds. It makes people harder to manipulate and easier to reach.

So yeah. One change.

Make humans insatiably, uncomfortably, beautifully curious again. Everything else gets better from there.
